See Appendix D.1 for proof. 3 Experiments and Results 3.1 Experimental setting Datasets and evaluation regimes. We evaluate FACET on protein-held-out HPA and OpenCell benchmarks. HPA contains 696 test images from 97 held-out proteins and provides nucleus, endoplasmic-reticulum, and microtubule context channels; we evaluate four compositions of these channels. OpenCell uses nucleus-only context and evaluates both HPA-adapted FACET , which transfers the HPA-trained FACET modules, and OpenCell-adapted FACET , which fits these modules on OpenCell data. Dataset construction and preprocessing are detailed in Appendix E . Metrics and statistics. Figure 2: Representative held-out HPA examples: morphology context, target, and model outputs. CELL-E2 uses nucleus-only context; CELL-Diff and FACET use all three context channels.

We report MI, MS-SSIM, Haralick texture agreement, PSNR, continuous spatial overlap ( IoU cont \mathrm{IoU}_{\mathrm{cont}} ), FID, and network function evaluations (NFE). IoU cont \mathrm{IoU}_{\mathrm{cont}} is the generalized Jaccard (Ruzicka) similarity. For protein-association pattern recovery, we report Pearson-similarity separation and Mann-Whitney U U tests; for predictive calibration, we report ECE, MCE, and Brier score. Metric definitions, aggregation, statistical tests, and sampling and calibration protocols are provided in Appendices F and G . Baselines and controls. We compare against two published generators, CELL-E2 ( Khwaja et al., 2023 ) and CELL-Diff ( Zheng and Huang, 2025 ) , as well as several backbone-matched internal baselines: ε \varepsilon -adaptation-only control, pathway and inference-time memory ablations, adaptation and initialization variants, and sampler variants across NFE budgets. To ensure that performance differences reflect FACET’s conditioning design rather than differences in backbone capacity or pretraining, all backbone-matched systems (CELL-Diff, FACET , and its internal variants) share the same pretrained ε \varepsilon -predictor, VAE, and ESM2 protein language model from the corresponding CELL-Diff checkpoint. CELL-Diff is, to our knowledge, the only public sequence-conditioned latent diffusion model with checkpoints for both benchmarks (Appendix E.3 ). In all FACET variants, the VAE and ESM2 remain frozen; the ε \varepsilon -predictor is either kept frozen or, in variants with backbone LoRA, adapted only through the introduced LoRA updates. 3.2 Conditional phenotype generation on HPA Table 1: Comparison on the HPA test set. Appendix E Experimental Setup and Data Preparation E.1 Human Protein Atlas benchmark The HPA benchmark is derived from the Human Protein Atlas ( Thul et al., 2017 ) . Each example contains a protein amino-acid sequence, a target protein-fluorescence image, and three cellular-context channels corresponding to the nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum (ER), and microtubules (MT). Images are cropped to 1024 × 1024 1024\times 1024 pixels and resized to 256 × 256 256\times 256 pixels before the frozen variational autoencoder (VAE) maps them to 4 × 64 × 64 4\times 64\times 64 latent representations. The released HPA training set contains 87,763 stored images from 12,732 proteins and the test split contains 720 stored images from 100 proteins 1 1 1 https://virtualcellmodels.cziscience.com/dataset/hpa-subcellular-section . Following Zheng and Huang (2025) , we use a maximum tokenized sequence length of 2048. This filtering removes 24 images from three proteins, yielding the 696-image, 97-protein evaluation set used throughout the paper. The longest retained sequence has 1938 residues, whereas the shortest excluded sequence has 2157 residues; therefore, the filtering boundary does not remove sequences close to the cutoff.

During FACET module adaptation and semantic memory construct, we use a random subset of the HPA training split, formed by adding whole proteins in a fixed random order until an image budget is reached and keeping every image of each selected protein. This yields 24,001 images from 3,491 of the 12,732 training proteins ( ≈ \approx 27% of training images); the pretrained backbone, in contrast, was trained on the full split. A protein-disjoint 10% of this pool (349 proteins, 2,467 images) forms a validation split that is excluded from every fit, is used only for hyperparameter tuning, and never overlaps the test proteins. Of the pool, 3,007 proteins carry a UniProt localization annotation; the 2,704 of them outside the validation split define the prototypes.
